query: For Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 initially in a high-temperature BCC state, the factors governing its phase stability during cooling and subsequent thermal exposure are not understood well enough to account for the range of phases that may appear. What single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain this behavior and why? Define a controlled comparison and baseline, predicted observations relative to that baseline, the conditions under which the hypothesis should and should not apply, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive falsification result.

generation.hypothesis: Thermal aging treatments applied at intermediate temperatures (specifically ~600°C for embrittlement and ~750°C for recovery) applied to AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA in as-cast state (FCC + B2 phases) will act through Enhanced L12 ordering (approaching perfect Ni3Al stoichiometry) in FCC domains coupled with the formation of jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries and Elevated APBE and elastic modulus in ordered domains restrict cross-slip and promote planar slip; combined with stress concentration at jagged PB tips, this triggers plastic instability. At higher temperatures, reduced ordering and formation of ductile transition zones along PBs restore ductility., giving A non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile transition where ductility is minimized at the aging temperature that maximizes L12 ordering and jagged PB density (600°C) and recovers at higher temperatures (750°C) where ordering is suppressed. relative to Conventional alloys exhibiting classical grain-boundary mediated thermal embrittlement (e.g., temper embrittlement via impurity segregation).
generation.material_initial_state: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA in as-cast state (FCC + B2 phases)
generation.intervention: Thermal aging treatments applied at intermediate temperatures (specifically ~600°C for embrittlement and ~750°C for recovery)
generation.conditions: Aging regime defined by a specific temperature window (approx. 550-750°C) where chemical ordering kinetics and phase boundary evolution are maximized
generation.structural_mediator: Enhanced L12 ordering (approaching perfect Ni3Al stoichiometry) in FCC domains coupled with the formation of jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries
generation.mechanism: Elevated APBE and elastic modulus in ordered domains restrict cross-slip and promote planar slip; combined with stress concentration at jagged PB tips, this triggers plastic instability. At higher temperatures, reduced ordering and formation of ductile transition zones along PBs restore ductility.
generation.predicted_outcome: A non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile transition where ductility is minimized at the aging temperature that maximizes L12 ordering and jagged PB density (600°C) and recovers at higher temperatures (750°C) where ordering is suppressed.
generation.baseline: Conventional alloys exhibiting classical grain-boundary mediated thermal embrittlement (e.g., temper embrittlement via impurity segregation)

falsification_experiment.design: Transmission Kikuchi Diffraction (TKD) or TEM observation of dislocation pile-ups and crack initiation specifically at the tips of jagged phase boundaries, with no evidence of intergranular impurity segregation.
measurements: Transmission Kikuchi Diffraction (TKD) or TEM observation of dislocation pile-ups and crack initiation specifically at the tips of jagged phase boundaries, with no evidence of intergranular impurity segregation.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the predicted outcome is not observed relative to the baseline, the hypothesis is rejected.
